texts.preamble: Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 Kabc0B0003822023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Sri. Vijaykumar S. Hiremath, Ll.B., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 08th Day of November 2024 M.V.C. No.1631/2023 C/W 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 Petitioner in Mr. Vinay R Mvc S/o Rajanna.
texts.facts: All these petitions are filed by the petitioners for the accidental injuries sustained by them in the road accident dated 17.01.2023. The petitioner in MVC No.1631/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-, MVC No.1632/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-, MVC No.1633/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- and petitioner in MVC No. 1634/2023 has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents with interest. Since all the petitions are arising out of the same accident and hence all the petitions are clubbed and common judgment is passed. SCCH-21 4 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 2. The Brief facts of the case of the petitioners in all the cases are as under: It is the case of the petitioners in all the cases were that on 17.01.2023 at about 10.15 a.m., the petitioner in MVC No.1631/2023 and his friends Yashavanth. M. E, Yashwanth. M and Vinith. H who are petitioners in MVC No.1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 were travelling in a Maruthi Omini bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-8578 driven by its driver slowly and cautiously and observing all traffic rules and regulations and movements of the vehicles from Devanahalli towards Nagarjuna Technical college on Chikkaballapura NH-44 road, when they reached near Attibele village U-turn, at that time, one Tipper Lorry bearing Reg. No. MP- 04-HE-1839 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner as endangers to human life, he came from left side and in order to Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153272833/ 3 took U-turn, near Attibele U-turn Junction, without giving any signal/indication at high speed and dashed against the Omini, due to forced impact the inmates of the Maruthi Omini were sustained grevious injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, the petitioners were shifted to New Manasa Hospital for first aid treatment and further shifted to Aveksha Hospital, Bangalore, wherein they were treated as inpatient and petitioners has spent SCCH-21 5 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 huge amount towards medical expenses. The petitioner in MVC No.1631/2023 submitted that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 19 years, the petitioner was Engineering student and also running tutorial and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. The petitioner in MVC No.1632/2023 submitted that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 21 years, the petitioner was Engineering student and also running tutorial and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. The petitioner in MVC No.1633/2023 submitted that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 19 years, the petitioner was Engineering student and also running tutorial and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. The petitioner in MVC No.1634/2023 submitted that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and aged about 19 years, the petitioner was Engineering student and also running tutorial and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioners Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153272833/ 4 have become permanently disabled and lost their future income. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the SCCH-21 6 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that the offending vehicle is insured with respondent No.2 and policy was inforce. Further the Registration certificate, Fitness Certificate, driving license of alleged vehicle were legally valid on accident date. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. This respondent accepts the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy. Further this respondent seeks protection u/s 134(c), 158(6) and 149(2) of M. V. Act. The first respondent had been willfully entrusted their vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license to drive the same as on the date of the accident. Further, this respondent submits that, the claim petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the owner SCCH-21 7 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 and insurer of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-05-ML-8578 which Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153272833/ 5 involved in the alleged accident is not made as parties to the claim petition. Further both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioners. The petitioners colluding with the owner and police filed the false cases. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioners in all the cases have been examined themselves as PW.1 to PW.4, Dr. Nagaraj. B. N is examined as PW.5 and also examined the M.R.O at Aveksha Hospital as PW.6 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.37 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents. Accordingly, the Vijayapura Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.009/2023. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs. 6,90,400/- under various heads.

The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153272833/ 16 evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N PW.5 who has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained traumatic L3 burst fracture & right ankle medical malleolus fracture and opined that, whole body physical disability with respect of the right ankle at 11% and that of total whole body physical disability at 28%. He was sworn that, petitioner has got 28% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability. During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioner argued that due to injury marriage prospectus of petitioner have been diminished. Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness as well as marriage prospectus. 33. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses. The doctor who has been examined as PW.5 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.40,000/-. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads: Vinay.R vs Dilip Buildcon Ltd on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153272833/ 18 38. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj. B. N in order to substantiate the same, SCCH-21 26 MVC No.1631/2023 C/w 1632, 1633 and 1634/2023 PW.5 who has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained left side open type II comminuted distal third humerus fracture with bone loss, lateral malleolus fracture right ankle and opined that, total disability of the left arm at 37% and that of whole body physical disability at 12%. He was sworn that, petitioner has got 12% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate. Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and Vinay. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
